# dotfiles

> Halit Sever's personal macOS dotfiles: an Oh My Zsh `.zshrc` (agnoster theme, git plugin) with PATH setup for Homebrew, Cargo, pnpm, the Android SDK and OpenJDK, optional pyenv, gvm and neofetch, git aliases and shared zsh history.

Install by cloning to `~/dotfiles` and symlinking: `ln -sf ~/dotfiles/.zshrc ~/.zshrc`. The paths assume macOS on Apple Silicon (Homebrew in `/opt/homebrew`, SDKs under `~/Library`), so the file needs edits before it works on Linux.

## Docs

- [Website](https://projects.halit.org/dotfiles/): the `.zshrc` annotated block by block, plus guides on `.zshrc`, aliases and dotfiles
- [Install Oh My Zsh on a Mac](https://projects.halit.org/dotfiles/install-oh-my-zsh-mac/): the official installer, the font agnoster needs, then this .zshrc with a backup and a symlink
- [Blog](https://projects.halit.org/dotfiles/blog/): zsh and Oh My Zsh guides
- [Choosing and switching a zsh theme with Oh My Zsh](https://projects.halit.org/dotfiles/blog/zsh-themes): How zsh themes work with Oh My Zsh: set ZSH_THEME, try random themes, install the font agnoster needs on a Mac, and add a theme Oh My Zsh does not bundle.
- [zsh is the shell, Oh My Zsh is a framework on top](https://projects.halit.org/dotfiles/blog/zsh-vs-oh-my-zsh): Zsh vs Oh My Zsh explained: one is the shell, the other a framework of themes, plugins and defaults. See what a real .zshrc takes from each and what to drop.
- [Zsh plugins: the git plugin and two common additions](https://projects.halit.org/dotfiles/blog/zsh-plugins): Which zsh plugins to install and how: the Oh My Zsh git plugin and its aliases, zsh-autosuggestions and zsh-syntax-highlighting, and plugin load order.
- [Powerlevel10k or agnoster: two powerline prompts compared](https://projects.halit.org/dotfiles/blog/powerlevel10k-vs-agnoster): Powerlevel10k vs agnoster on Oh My Zsh: install steps, fonts, the p10k configure wizard, instant prompt, and the limited support notice in the p10k README.
- [Reloading .zshrc: source, exec zsh and omz reload](https://projects.halit.org/dotfiles/blog/reload-zshrc): How to reload .zshrc after an edit: source ~/.zshrc, exec zsh or omz reload, what each one does to PATH and aliases, and a reload alias that does not pile up.
- [zsh: command not found after a .zshrc change](https://projects.halit.org/dotfiles/blog/zshrc-command-not-found): Fix zsh command not found errors after editing .zshrc: read the error line, check PATH order for Homebrew and pnpm, rehash, and test the file with zsh -n.
- [Which zsh startup file to use: .zshrc, .zprofile or .zshenv](https://projects.halit.org/dotfiles/blog/zshrc-vs-zprofile): zshrc vs zprofile vs zshenv: the order zsh reads its startup files, login and interactive shells on macOS, where PATH belongs, and how bash files compare.
- [Removing Oh My Zsh and getting your old .zshrc back](https://projects.halit.org/dotfiles/blog/uninstall-oh-my-zsh): Uninstall Oh My Zsh with uninstall_oh_my_zsh: what the script deletes, how it restores .zshrc.pre-oh-my-zsh, symlinked dotfiles, and what to use instead.
- [README](https://github.com/halitsever/dotfiles/blob/main/Readme.md): features and install steps
- [.zshrc](https://github.com/halitsever/dotfiles/blob/main/.zshrc): the zsh configuration itself
- [CI workflow](https://github.com/halitsever/dotfiles/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml): the `zsh -n` syntax check run on every push and pull request
